question: Can a class-balanced detached counterfactual branch-preference objective calibrate the causal call gate without changing the memory or adding inference-time oracle inputs?

source_checkpoint.reason: C4 learned a small, consistently positive ranking correction over C3 static call but left all probabilities near one.

objective.name: class-balanced detached counterfactual call preference
objective.branch_error: per-token RGB pixel MSE under teacher-forced causal history
objective.label: memory preferred iff static-HPC pixel error is lower; PFC preferred iff PFC-only pixel error is lower
objective.loss: 0.5 * softplus(-call_logit) on memory-preferred tokens + 0.5 * softplus(call_logit) on PFC-preferred tokens

model_inputs: causal PFC and HPC internal features

registered_conditions: C5 hard invocation at fixed threshold 0.5
C4 soft probability on identical slice
C3 static call on identical slice

acceptance_gates: every smoke and training batch contains both memory-preferred and PFC-preferred tokens after the fixed gap filter
preference loss and gradients remain finite
all non-gate checkpoint tensors remain bitwise identical to C4
C5 hard threshold-0.5 beats paired PFC-only by at least 2% relative
paired-bootstrap 90% lower bound of PFC-only minus C5 hard error is above zero
C5 hard improves over C4 soft by at least 0.5% relative on the identical fresh slice
C5 hard episode-gain p10 removes at least 25% of the C3 static negative p10 shortfall
C5 hard call rate lies between 0.1 and 0.9
future ground-truth reads and writes remain zero

decision_rule.advance: If every gate passes, replicate C5 from a second call-gate initialization.
decision_rule.soft_only: If C5 soft passes the main PFC gates but hard invocation fails, retain only the soft router claim and do not call it discrete invocation.
decision_rule.classification_fail: If teacher preference accuracy improves but rollout does not, reject teacher-forced preference as distribution-mismatched and move to rollout counterfactual labels.
decision_rule.stop: If neither hard nor soft improves over C4, retain C4 as the final call policy and stop router tuning.
